$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: Land Under an Unfamiliar Sky

goal.text: Find your feet on an island high in the sky.

steps.label: Learn to listen for a rift
Help the keeper guard the edge
Find which way the song leads

plate.narration: High above the realm, stone islands drift like slow boats. Gold-roofed temples glow on their backs. Roots dangle into the clouds, and wind banners snap in every direction at once.

island.narration: The fold opens onto cold stone high above the realm. Your party stumbles through together. Behind you the fold shuts with a pop, and wind rushes in to fill the gap. A kitsune temple keeper hooks one arm through a rope ring and waves you over. "Hold on to something! These are called the Sky Islands, and this one is not where it belongs." Your goal is to find your feet up here. Find shelter, listen for the opening, and help her mark the unsafe path.

choices.label: Grab a ring and hold on

variants.text: The Cairnstep griffins swoop low and set your whole party down on a stone pad high above the realm. They are gone again in three flaps. A kitsune temple keeper hooks one arm through a rope ring and waves you over. "Hold on to something! These are called the Sky Islands. Our old landing route points into empty sky now." Your goal is to find your feet up here. Find shelter, listen for the opening, and help her mark the unsafe path.

landing.prompt: The wind hits the landing pad like a slammed door. Everyone grab a rope ring and hold on!

landing_held.narration: Every hand finds a ring. The gust howls over your heads and moves on. The keeper counts you with her chin. "Good grips. Most visitors arrive by sitting down hard." She leads you past a gold-roofed shrine with a bronze bell as big as a barrel. Wind banners snap above it, each one pointing a different way. "Walk where I walk," she says. "Ask questions when both feet are happy." She presses a wrapped supper bundle into your hands. "Eat when the wind lets you."

choices.label: Follow the keeper

landing_slid.narration: The wind scoops your whole party off its feet. You slide across the boards like soap. The keeper flings her rope and hooks the last boot an arm's length from the edge. Everyone is safe, if scraped. Your hats keep going. One lands on a passing gull, which now looks very official. "Welcome," says the keeper, dusting off her tails. "That is how the pad says hello." She tosses you a wrapped supper bundle for the scrapes.

choices.label: Get up and follow the keeper

lesson.narration: A kitsune named Seren Wisp is comparing notes with a young manticore named Pip Thistledown. They wear the Riftseekers' clasps. "I am counting what has moved," says Pip, tapping his notebook. "The count keeps changing. Help me and you can read it." Seren asks you to hum the hall note, then listen for an answering sound. "A starweaver can learn to answer a rift's hum. That is called Attune. No one here chooses a rift's rules."

choices.label: Hum the hall note and listen
Ask Pip to show his notebook first
Answer the hum with Attune

variants.text: A kitsune named Seren Wisp and a manticore named Pip Thistledown are checking another displaced route. They wear the Riftseekers' clasps. Pip taps his notebook. "The count keeps changing here too. Help me and you can read it." Seren asks you to compare the sounds with what she taught you before.

pip_notes.narration: Pip opens his notebook with both paws. It is full of tiny islands and arrows that have been crossed out. "This one was east of here at breakfast. Now it is south, and the arrow is too small to show how rude that is." He taps a smudge. "There is a sound out there, and when it moves, the islands near it move too. I think. I cannot prove it alone. Will you help me listen?"

choices.label: Listen with Seren

hum.prompt: Hum the hall note, then listen hard. Which way does the answering sound come from?

hum_attuned.prompt: A starweaver leads the Attune answer, humming back to the rift. The qualified hero assists; choose who leads the team check.

hum_heard.narration: A thin hum answers from far to the east. Then it answers again from the very same spot. You point. Seren's ears swing up. "That is a rift talking. Its hum stays put while the wind runs around it. Remember the feel of it. A hum is steady. Wind is a liar." Pip writes EAST in his notebook and underlines it twice, in case east moves.

choices.label: Look at the island

hum_fuzzy.narration: The wind drowns your note, and your answer comes out a jumble. Seren does not sigh. She hums slowly, then has you press a palm flat to the stone. You feel it, low and steady, a hum in your hand instead of your ears. It takes longer, and it sticks. Pip writes EAST with a question mark and gives the question mark a tiny hat.

choices.label: Look at the island

local.narration: The keeper shows you a rope stretched between two marker posts. Yesterday it pointed toward a neighboring island. Now it points into empty sky, and travelers keep following it. A low song sounds beyond the mist. How will you help her keep travelers clear of the edge?

choices.label: Move the warning markers to the path
Listen for the song before marking the path
Scout the edge from the air

markers.narration: The keeper has three cairn stones, each as heavy as a sleeping goat. They belong on the path, where a traveler will see them before the rope road ends. The boards are slick with mist, and the wind keeps trying to help. Each stone rides a wooden sledge. Someone strong must pull, and the rest must keep the sledge straight.

choices.label: Start dragging

markers_check.prompt: Drag the cairn stones along the slick path. The strongest of you pulls, and the rest steady the sledge.

markers_set.narration: Three cairns stand in a line, tall enough to see in fog. The keeper ties a warning cord between them and plucks it. It hums. "One less traveler walking toward an old view." She pats the nearest cairn as if it were a pony, and the cairn, being a rock, says nothing. Pip salutes it anyway, just in case it is somebody important.

choices.label: Go on

markers_dropped.narration: The last stone slides off its sledge, rolls to the edge, and drops out of sight. You wait for a crash. Nothing comes. "It will arrive somewhere," says the keeper. She ties her own washing line between the two cairns you saved and clips a spoon to it. The spoon clatters in the wind, which is more warning than you expected.

choices.label: Go on

song.narration: You wait until the low song sounds again. It travels through the mist from a spot far from where the keeper expected. She hands you her slate and a stub of chalk. "Mark where it comes from, every time it sounds. Everyone points at once. If most of you agree, we have a true bearing."

choices.label: Point together

song_check.prompt: Everyone points at the sound each time it comes. If most of you agree, the keeper can chalk a true bearing.

song_bearing.narration: Most fingers point the same way: east, and a little down. The keeper chalks a bold line on her slate, then a second line to show where the old route pointed. They do not agree at all. "So the song is not where it was," she says. "Neither are we." She moves the marker posts to match your line, and hangs her spare scarf on one to make it feel important. The scarf flaps toward the east, as if it agrees.

choices.label: Go on

song_muddled.narration: Fingers point east, south, and one straight up at a gull. The slate looks as if a spider fell in the chalk. The keeper rubs it out with her sleeve, kindly. "The song bounces off the mist. We will catch it again when the sky is calmer." She picks one guess, east, and moves the marker posts to it. The gull looks insulted.

choices.label: Go on

edge_scout.prompt: Wings lift you over the edge. Can the best flier hold steady in the gusts long enough to see the whole island?

edge_scouted.narration: From up here the island looks like a dropped cookie: a shrine, a landing pad, a tall pole with an iron basket on top, and a rope road that runs to nothing. Beyond the mist a long shape slides by, far away, singing. You land and draw the keeper a map in the dust. Cairns here, here and here. She nods so hard her ears flap.

choices.label: Go on

edge_gusted.narration: A gust spins you like a leaf. You tumble back to the pad with a bump, wings flapping, dignity gone. You saw enough to know the edge is longer than the rope. The keeper drags three cairns to the path herself, muttering, and you help her set them where you remember. They lean a little, like friends telling a secret.

choices.label: Go on

walker.narration: A rattle comes down the old rope road. A kite seller is pulling a cart of kites toward the edge, his eyes on the sky and his nose in a map. The map is upside down. The road ends in empty air twenty steps ahead of him. "Dob!" shouts the keeper. "Stop!" The kite seller waves cheerfully and keeps walking. How will you stop him?

choices.label: Sprint down the boards and grab his cart rope
Wave the warning cord and call him back
Leap ahead and block the road

walker_catch.prompt: Sprint down the slick boards and catch the cart's rope before the front wheel reaches the last plank.

walker_call.prompt: Wave the warning cord and call his name, loud and kind, until he looks up from his upside-down map.

walker_leap.prompt: Leap carries you over the cart and onto the last plank. Can you land square and turn the cart around?

walker_safe.narration: Dob stops, one wheel on the last plank, and looks down. He looks up. He looks at his map, and turns it right side up. "Ah," he says. The keeper does not scold. She makes him tea he forgets to drink. "I sell kites to the island across," says Dob. "The road went wrong, and I did not. I think." He unrolls a bundle of bright kite-flags with long tails. "You saved my cart. Wave these, and the whole sky will see." He ties a springy kite-string lace around your ankle. "For quick feet." Then he counts four coins into your hand, with a bow.

choices.label: Go on

walker_dragged.narration: The cart tips at the last plank, one wheel in the sky. You and the keeper haul on the rope while kites spill off like startled birds. A few escape. Most snag on the posts. Dob dangles from his strap, smiling, his hat gone. "Ah," he says. "Wrong road." Back on stone, he gathers what is left, a bundle of bright kite-flags with long tails. "I sell kites to the island across. Wave these, and the whole sky will see." He presses three coins into your hand, all he can find in his pockets.

choices.label: Go on

edge_merge.narration: The keeper leans on a rope ring and studies the sky. Dob sits on his cart with his map the right way up. "Good. That is the edge told about, and one kite seller safe. Now the hard part." She points to a tall pole with an iron basket on top. "The signal basket. At dusk we light it, so every island and ferry knows where we hang. The pole is crooked from the move, and our fuel is a mess. A ferry captain named Thimble is due tonight with passengers, and without a light she will never find us."

choices.label: Cross the pad to the pole

basket_plan.narration: The pole leans like a sleepy giraffe. Its stone foot has cracked loose from the rock. Pip circles it twice, chewing his pencil. "If that tips at dusk, the fire goes over the edge and the basket goes with it." The keeper hands you a coil of rope and a pile of wedge stones. Raise it straight and make it firm before dark. How will you do it?

choices.label: Raise it with ropes, everyone hauling
Fit wedge stones under the foot, one careful try at a time
Lift it upright with Smash
Brace the foot while friends tie off the ropes

pole_ropes.prompt: Loop the ropes around the pole and haul. Everyone heaves together on the keeper's count!

pole_wedge.prompt: Find the wedge stones that fit the cracked foot. Which stone goes where, and in what order?

pole_smash.prompt: Smash lifts the pole upright. Can you seat the stone foot back in its socket without cracking it again?

pole_brace.prompt: Brace holds the foot steady. Can the others tie off the guy ropes before the pole shifts?

pole_up.narration: The pole stands straight as a spoon in porridge. The basket sits level on top. The keeper taps it, and it gives a proud, tinny ring. Pip, who held one rope end a moment too long, is lifted half a step off the ground. He does not mention it. Neither does anyone else, loudly. The wind banners, annoyed, all turn to point at the pole.

choices.label: Go on

pole_leaning.narration: The pole stands, mostly. It leans a thumb's width to the east and creaks at every gust. The keeper ties on two extra guy ropes and gives it a stern look. "It will hold. It just has opinions." Whoever lights the basket will need to keep a steady hand while the pole sways.

choices.label: Go on

fuel.narration: There is no fire without fuel. The oil jars cracked in the move, and the keeper's store is a sad shiny puddle. She points two ways. A woodshed under the shrine eaves holds dry logs, if you can carry them across the yard. The orchard has fresh windfall twigs, if you can catch them. The wind wants both. What will you fetch?

choices.label: Haul dry logs from the woodshed
Chase the windfall twigs in the orchard
Let a duskrunner dash for the dry logs
Tie on Dob's lace and run for the dry logs

fuel_logs.prompt: Carry the dry logs across the yard. The wind shoves at every armful, and the logs want to roll away.

fuel_twigs.prompt: Dash after the windfall twigs before the wind scatters them over the edge. Grab and stuff them in your sacks!

fuel_lace.prompt: Dob's springy lace on your ankle makes your feet light. Race the gusts to the dry logs and bring them back.

fuel_dash.prompt: A duskrunner's speed gets to the dry logs before the next gust. Can the rest of you keep the armfuls from tumbling?

fuel_dry.narration: You stack the fuel at the foot of the pole. Dry wood smells like a warm kitchen, even in a gale. The keeper counts the logs with one finger, nods, and counts them again for luck. Pip offers to carry the last twig. It is the size of a pencil. He carries it like a sword. The keeper tucks a dry twig behind her ear for later, and promptly forgets it is there.

choices.label: Go on

fuel_soggy.narration: Half the wood is wet, and the other half is wetter. It will smoke when it should crackle. The keeper holds up a log and sniffs it, unhappy. "This will burn. It will not like it." She trades you a bundle of dry shrine incense to help it along. "Do not tell the shrine," she whispers, glancing at the bronze bell.

choices.label: Go on

light.narration: The sun slides behind the mist, and the sky turns the color of weak tea. The basket is full. Now someone must light it in a gale. The keeper holds out a flint striker in one paw and a clay pot of shrine coals in the other. Seren checks the wind with a wet finger. "Fast and bright, or slow and careful," she says. "Both can work, if nobody sneezes." Which will you try?

choices.label: Strike sparks while everyone shields the basket
Pass the pot of coals hand to hand up the ladder
Call fox fire into the basket

light_flint.prompt: Strike the flint while everyone cups cloaks and hands around the sparks, each of you on a different side of the basket.

light_coals.prompt: Pass the pot hand to hand up the ladder, steady and calm. Anyone with shaky hands will spill the coals.

light_fox.prompt: Little fox fire dances into the basket. Can you coax it to sit in the wood and hold, even when the pole sways?

basket_lit.narration: The flame catches, flares, and stands up tall and gold. The whole basket glows like a lantern. Far off in the mist, a tiny answering light blinks once, twice. The keeper's face unclenches. "There. Now the sky can find us." The edge is told about, and lit. For the first time the island feels like a place on a map. Pip bows to the basket, and the basket, being on fire, glows politely back. The keeper hands you a brass whistle from the shrine. "One loud note, for when the sky needs to hear you."

choices.label: Watch the basket

basket_smoky.narration: The wood sulks, then smokes, then gives a small orange flame that coughs at every gust. It is lit, which is the main thing. The keeper feeds it a handful of shrine incense and it brightens to a wobbly glow that smells faintly of lemon cake. It will be seen. It just will not be seen smoothly.

choices.label: Watch the basket

dusk_ferry.narration: Something drops out of the dusk and lands on the pole rail hard enough to rattle the basket. It is a griffin with a satchel and a very ruffled neck. "Fenwick, courier! Every island in the sky has been hunting for your light." He flaps a wing at the mist. "Captain Thimble's ferry is right behind me. The wind is swinging her sideways, and her passengers are shouting. She needs a landing now." How will you bring her in?

choices.label: Catch the ferry's trailing lines and tie them off
Wave her in with Dob's kite-flags
Fly out and tow her line
Brace the mooring post against the pull
Blow the brass whistle so she can steer by it

variants.text: "The Cairnstep watchers told me where you landed," he adds. "They said to look after you."

ferry_lines.prompt: Snatch the ferry's trailing lines as they whip past the pad, and loop them around the mooring posts.

ferry_flags.prompt: The sharpest eyes read the ferry's heading through the mist and call which kite-flags to wave. Left, right, hold.

ferry_tow.prompt: Wings take you out over the gap. Can the best flier catch the line and pull the ferry straight?

ferry_whistle.prompt: One loud brass note rolls out over the gap. Call the ferry in with it, note by note, so she steers straight to the pad.

ferry_post.prompt: Brace holds the post steady. Can the others haul the ferry in hand over hand before the wind swings her out?

ferry_in.narration: The ferry thumps against the pad and stays there. Hens flap out of a basket and walk about with complete confidence. Out steps a kitsune in a windblown coat, a captain's hat held on with string. "Captain Thimble. Best landing I have had all week, and that includes my own." Behind her, passengers cling to the rail, loudly refusing to let go. Thimble looks at you and then at the sky. "I need a safe lane home for everyone aboard, and a very strong cup of tea."

choices.label: Help the passengers off
Share your supper with the passengers first

variants.text: Then she stops and stares. "You! You found us. I told you to look for the washing." A line of damp socks flaps from the ferry rail.

ferry_bumped.narration: The ferry swings, bumps the pad, and bounces off like a ball. A crate of washing hops over the rail and spills socks across the pad. Hens flap out in all directions and walk about with complete confidence. Out steps a kitsune in a windblown coat, a captain's hat held on with string. "Captain Thimble. I have had worse landings. Not this week." Her passengers cling to the rail, loudly refusing to let go. Thimble looks at you and then at the sky. "I need a safe lane home for everyone aboard, and a very strong cup of tea."

choices.label: Help the passengers off
Share your supper with the passengers first

variants.text: She stops and stares. "You! You found us. I told you to look for the washing." She waves a sock at you, then at the pad.

passengers.prompt: The passengers will not leave the rail, and Thimble cannot think over the noise. Calm them and coax them off the ferry.

passengers_fed.narration: You pass the wrapped supper around. A hungry passenger sniffs it, then smiles. One by one the passengers let go of the rail, just to hold a piece of bread. The keeper sends them to the shrine for barley tea, and the hens follow, in a line. Thimble drops onto a barrel, finally quiet enough to think.

choices.label: Sit with Thimble

passengers_calm.narration: You speak softly and offer a steady hand. One by one the passengers let go of the rail and step onto firm stone. The keeper sends them to the shrine for barley tea. The hens follow, in a line, as if they had planned it. Thimble drops onto a barrel, finally quiet enough to think.

choices.label: Sit with Thimble

passengers_stuck.narration: The passengers cling harder. The keeper has to bring a ladder, then a blanket, then a plate of rice crackers, and finally the passengers climb down, one crunch at a time. It takes ages. Thimble drops onto a barrel, worn out and still slightly shouted at. "Next time," she says, "I bring only hens."

choices.label: Sit with Thimble

thimble.narration: Thimble unrolls a chart, held flat by three hens. "My old lane is gone, and my passengers want to go home. I used to steer by the cloud whales' song. Wherever they sing, the sky stays level and a ferry can cross. Now the song has wandered." She lays a paw on the ferry's rail. It hums faintly, and the hum leans east. Fenwick holds a feather beside it, and the feather leans east too. "Flags have no word for 'the sky has moved,'" he says. "But you can ask the air." Thimble nods. "Find the whales, and you find my lane. Find where the song comes from, and Fenwick will carry the news to every island in the sky."

choices.label: Rest by the wind wall

windbreak_rest.narration: The keeper builds a wind wall of baskets and blankets behind the shrine. Hot barley tea goes around in chipped cups. The hens roost on Pip, who bears it nobly. Far off, the low song comes again, slower than before. Seren says the next part is the hardest to hear and the easiest to miss. Everyone gets warm. Dob has hung his kites along the wind wall like laundry, and a ribbon cart sits open beside the fire.

choices.label: Sit by the fire and rest
Help Pip dry his notebook
Buy a songbird ribbon from Dob's cart (3 coins)
Mend the day's scrapes first

pip_night.narration: Pip's notebook is soaked at one corner. You lay the pages by the fire, and Pip reads you his list aloud, with feeling: islands that moved, three socks, a hen named Gravy. "I do not know why it is all moving," he says quietly. "I only know it is easier to count with friends." The hen named Gravy agrees, from his head.

choices.label: Settle down for the night

night_song.narration: Night. The sky is huge and full of stars, and one drifting lantern, which is Pip's. The shrine bell shivers all by itself. The keeper brings out her slate, crowded with chalk lines of where things used to be. Then the low song comes, close and slow, rolling over the island like a wave. The keeper sets down her cup. "That is the nearest it has been. Tonight we find which way it leads. If we can name the singer, we can help the singer, and maybe my island too."

choices.label: Follow the song

bearing_vote.narration: Everyone has a piece. There is the hum you listened for this morning, the keeper's chalk slate, Thimble's ferry rail, Fenwick's feather, and Pip's notebook of crossed-out arrows. Laid together, they should show where the song leads. Seren waits with her tail curled around her feet. Where will you start?

choices.label: Lay Pip's notebook over the keeper's slate
Ring the edge with feathers and lanterns, and call out
Hum back, low and long, and listen for the answer
Ring your listening chime and listen for its echo

bearing_notes.prompt: The sharpest mind lines up the crossed-out arrows with the chalk lines until one direction wins.

bearing_air.prompt: Each of you takes a place around the edge with a feather or a lantern. Call out when yours leans, and see if most of you agree.

bearing_chime.prompt: Ring the listening chime beside the song. An echo that leans one way shows where the song leads. Can you read it?

bearing_sing.prompt: A songkeeper hums back, low and long, and listens for how the answer returns. The qualified hero assists; choose who leads the team check.

bearing_found.narration: All the pieces point one way: east, past the dark edge, to a place where the sky is singing. Thimble taps her chart. Fenwick fluffs his feathers. The keeper smiles for the first time since you landed. "The old keepers said the cloud whales sing where the sky is safe to cross. If they are singing there, then something has changed there, and they will need help before we do. Someone must go and see. It is a long way for a ferry and a short way for a kind heart."

choices.label: Listen as the song comes closer

bearing_blurred.narration: The pieces almost fit. Seren sets them out again, patient as a cat. Then it clicks: the feather, the rail, the notebook, the chalk. East, past the dark edge, to a place where the sky is singing. It takes most of the night. Fenwick says you were close, and that he would say so either way. "Cloud whales," the keeper says. "The old keepers said they sing where the sky is safe to cross. If they are singing there, something has changed, and they will need help before we do. Someone must go and see. It is a long way for a ferry and a short way for a kind heart."

choices.label: Listen as the song comes closer

route_vote.narration: Dawn is a pale stripe. The ferry creaks at its ropes, and Fenwick stretches one wing, then the other. The keeper folds a flag-cloth stamped with her island's mark and presses it into your hands. "Someone must go and see what is wrong with the singing. Thimble's ferry can take you part of the way. Fenwick can lead you along the stepping islands." How will you go?

choices.label: Ride the ferry with Captain Thimble
Follow Fenwick along the stepping islands

route_ferry.narration: Thimble hands out boarding ropes. "Hold the rail with both hands, and do not sing back until I say." Her passengers have voted to stay with the keeper, hens included, in case there is more barley tea. Dob has loaded his cart of kites aboard, and sits on top of it with his map the right way up. The keeper tucks her island's flag-cloth into your pack and pats it twice, for luck.

choices.label: Go to the landing pad

route_flags.narration: Fenwick pulls three tiny flags from his satchel and clips them to his wing. "Steady air, steady air, steady air. I will fly ahead and wave. If I wave two, hold onto something." The keeper tucks her island's flag-cloth into your pack and pats it twice, for luck. A hen watches, deeply unimpressed. Dob will wait for the ferry to come back, selling kites to anyone brave enough to look up.

choices.label: Go to the landing pad

island_done.narration: Dawn. The island falls away behind you, small and gold-roofed, its signal basket still glowing. The low song rolls in from the east, slow and wide. Far off, a huge shape moves gently through the mist, singing. The cloud whales are out there. You have neighbors who trust you, a bearing, and a route to follow.

variants.text: The ferry hums under your feet.
Fenwick circles ahead, his flags snapping, already pointing the way.
Captain Thimble waves her string-tied hat from the rail. "Told you!" she calls. "You cannot miss the washing!"

gust_lull.narration: Between you and the pole lies the open pad, and the wind comes in gusts. When a gust is done, every wind banner droops at once. Pip counts the gusts out loud and loses count. The keeper points. "Wait for the lull, then cross."

interaction.cue: Wait until the banners droop, then run to the pole.

onSuccess.narration: The banners droop, and you cross in one long stride. The wind holds its breath until you arrive.

onFailure.narration: A gust spins you twice and sits you down. The keeper reels you in on her rope, and you reach the pole dizzy and cheerful.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper calls the lull for you. "Now!" You cross together without a single stumble.

fuel_chain.narration: The fuel must reach the basket at the top of the pole, and the ladder only fits one at a time. The keeper stands at the bottom and Pip waits at the top, holding his arms out like a very small harbor. Pass each log hand to hand, and do not drop one on the keeper.

interaction.cue: Catch the logs and pass them up the line.

onSuccess.narration: Pip drops the last log into the basket with a clunk and a cheer. Nobody is hit. The keeper counts this as a miracle.

onFailure.narration: One log escapes and rolls under the shrine. The keeper fetches it, grumbling nicely, and the basket is full anyway.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper hauls the last logs up on a rope and ties them off with a bow. "A little help is still help," she says.

camp_play.narration: Everyone settles in behind the wind wall. The keeper asks what would make this a good camp tonight. Pip suggests more hens. The hens, listening, suggest more barley. Add something to the camp, one at a time.

interaction.cue: Add something to your cozy camp.

options.label: Hang a kite as a lantern shade
options.reaction: The kite glows like a paper moon, and the wind banners all lean in to look.

options.label: Pour hot barley tea
options.reaction: Steam curls up in the lantern light. A hen leans in for the smell.

options.label: Spread a thick blanket
options.reaction: The blanket fills with wind for a moment, then settles like a sleepy cat.

options.label: Tell a short, funny story
options.reaction: Pip laughs so hard he knocks his own pencil into the fire pit. It is rescued, slightly toasted.

onSuccess.narration: The camp glows. For one quiet minute the island does not feel lost at all.

onFailure.narration: The camp is a little lopsided and the hens are in the middle of it. It is perfect anyway.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper adds the last touches herself, humming. The camp is cozy before you know it.

song_track.narration: The low song makes a faint glow in one of three wind-bells on the shrine's edge. The glow hops from bell to bell like a flea. Seren holds a hand up for quiet. "Watch it. Wherever it ends is the way the song leads."

interaction.cue: Watch the glow hop between the bells, then pick where it ends.

onSuccess.narration: The glow settles in the east bell and stays there, humming. East, the bells agree.

onFailure.narration: You pick the wrong bell, and the east bell rings out cheerfully all by itself. East, then.

onAssisted.narration: Seren points at the east bell, steady as a signpost. "There. Now you know what to prove."

song_echo.narration: The song comes again, closer than ever, in a pattern: low, high, low, middle. Thimble says it is how the whales say here we are. Seren says to answer in the same pattern, so they know a friend is listening. The shrine bell hangs ready, with three notes.

interaction.cue: Watch the pattern, then ring it back on the bell.

onSuccess.narration: The song stops. Then it answers with one long, warm note from the east. Seren grins. "They heard us."

onFailure.narration: Your pattern wobbles, but the song answers anyway, patient as a grown-up answering a very small question.

onAssisted.narration: Seren rings along and steadies each note. The song answers, long and warm, from the east.

wisps.narration: The brighter the basket glows, the more the dusk fills with little floating lights. Two wisps tumble in on the gale, tiny and ghostly, and circle the flame like moths. They tug at it and giggle. They think the fire is a very large, very rude candle, and they want it for themselves. The wind pulls the flame sideways. The keeper grabs her rope. "They will tear it apart! Shoo them off, gently!"

choices.label: Shoo the wisps away

wisp_fight.narration: The wisps zip in circles around the pole and dive at the flame. Drive them away from the basket before the gale and their tugging pull the fire apart.

wisps_shooed.narration: The wisps squeak, wobble, and bob away over the edge, still giggling. The flame stands straight again. Pip, who has a jar for everything, catches a spoonful of their soft leftover glow and screws on the lid. "For emergencies," he says. "Or snacks." The keeper laughs so hard her ears flap.

choices.label: Watch the sky

wisps_rescued.narration: The wisps swirl around you until the world is all dizzy sparkles. The keeper rings the shrine bell with both paws. Wisps hate a loud, honest bell, and they scatter into the dusk with a rude little pop. The keeper wraps everyone in blankets and passes round hot tea. Nobody gets a jar of glow tonight, but the basket is still burning, a little singed and very proud.

choices.label: Watch the sky

island_rest.narration: The ferry creaks at the landing pad, and Fenwick stretches his wings in the first light. Beside the pad stands a stone hut. Its door rattles in the wind. Thump. Something soft hits the wall inside. Far off, a huge shape moves through the mist, singing. You can knock, or you can set out for the cloud whales.

choices.label: Knock on the stone hut's door
Say your goodbyes and set out

dojo.narration: A bigfoot named Master Dunnick opens the door a crack and pulls you in out of the wind. Then he leans his back against it. The wind pushes. He pushes back. He has held this door shut for forty years. "This school is called the Dojo," he says. "Here we train the Thornguard, a hero who holds the line." A thorn bracer hangs on a hook by the fire. A Thornguard's strength lives in that bracer, and a song bell worn beside it will not ring. Thump. In the corner, students are catching pillows as they drop from the rafters. "Anyone who wants the bracer," says Master Dunnick, "may try it on."

variants.text: Master Dunnick is still leaning on the door of the Dojo. "Back already? Good. The wind never stops, so neither do we." The thorn bracer waits on its hook for anyone who wants to try it on. Thump. Another pillow drops.

choices.label: Catch the falling pillows
Back to the sheltered path

dojo_pillows.narration: A student unties a rope. Pillows tumble from the rafters. You plant your feet and catch one, then another, then another. The next one lands on your head. Master Dunnick nods without leaving the door. "That is how you brace. Stand still, and let it come to you."

choices.label: Back to the sheltered path

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
